text.arabic_uthmani: ۞ قُلْ إِنِّى نُهِيتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَمَّا جَآءَنِىَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتُ مِن رَّبِّى وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أُسْلِمَ لِرَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ

words.gloss_range: commanded public saying that governs the whole declaration
words.root_gloss_range: saying, declaration, and accountable verbal stance
words.prose: With {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}), the ayah begins in commissioned speech: the following first-person refusal is not self-authored rhetoric but a declaration the messenger is ordered to voice. The word makes the worship boundary public and accountable, and its opening position places prohibition, proof, and submission under one speech command. The worship-boundary address also resonates with the commanded address of 109:1, while the local ayah adds the proof-arrival warrant.

topics.headline: imperative governs the quoted declaration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first-person testimony is delivered under an order to speak, not as detached autobiography.
topics.reason: The aligned word is an imperative speech verb governing the quoted content in the attachment evidence.

topics.headline: speech makes the boundary public
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the refusal of rival worship is voiced as accountable doctrine rather than kept as private aversion.
topics.reason: The root field supports saying and declaration, while local discourse makes the statement public.

topics.headline: commanded address joins a known refusal pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a worship-boundary address comparable to 109:1, with this ayah adding the arrival of proofs as warrant.
topics.reason: The cited intertextual rows connect the opening command with worship-separation formulae, especially 109:1.

topics.headline: opening command frames the whole sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah as an ordered sequence: speech, prohibition, proof-arrival, and positive command.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the following utterance as the quoted complement of the command.

topics.headline: compact opening sound
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The sound note adds little beyond the retained opening-command payoff.
topics.reason: The sound note adds little beyond the retained opening-command payoff.

words.gloss_range: emphatic first-person assertion attached to the following passive predicate
words.prose: {{ar:إِنِّى}} ({{tr:innī}}) fuses confirmation with the speaker’s own “I,” so the passive prohibition is personally borne without becoming self-legislated before an audience whose invocation practice is being rejected. After the opening command, the discourse shifts into quoted first-person testimony: obedience to the command and personal dissociation from rival worship arrive together.

topics.headline: emphasis attaches the passive to the speaker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the claim is both confirmed and personally routed to the speaker.
topics.reason: The particle-plus-suffix construction is the internal subject frame for the following passive predicate.

topics.headline: confirmation meets the audience practice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the assertion is strengthened before an audience whose own invocation practice is being rejected.
topics.reason: The discourse profile makes the emphatic assertion apt in a contested address.

topics.headline: second person command becomes first person testimony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the person shift from ordered messenger to quoted witness.
topics.reason: The local clause architecture moves from the imperative into the speaker-bound report.

words.gloss_range: completed passive prohibition imposed on the speaker against the following worship act
words.root_gloss_range: forbidding, stopping, restraining, and endpoint or boundary imagery
words.prose: {{ar:نُهِيتُ}} ({{tr:nuhītu}}) presents the refusal as a restraint already imposed on the speaker. The passive form foregrounds the one restrained while veiling the forbidding agent, so the boundary against rival worship is received rather than invented. The root’s stopping-field makes that boundary feel like an endpoint before worship can cross it; restraint of desire in 79:40 becomes, here, restraint of worship-direction toward rivals. The paired passive later supplies the positive command that answers the prohibition.

topics.headline: settled passive prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speaker stands under an already imposed restraint before addressing the audience.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify a perfect passive first-person verb governing the following complement.

topics.headline: restraint as boundary and stopping-place
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the prohibition as a stopping boundary, while local grammar keeps the selected sense as being forbidden.
topics.reason: The root family supports stopping and boundary pressure, but the local passive selects prohibition.

topics.headline: self-restraint becomes worship-restraint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare restraint of desire in 79:40 with restraint of worship-direction here, without letting that parallel control the local parse.
topics.reason: The cited rows make 79:40 a concrete contrast for the n-h-y restraint field.

topics.headline: prohibition pairs with command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a two-sided mandate: one act is blocked and another is commissioned.
topics.reason: The ayah repeats first-person passive mandate language across the negative and positive halves.

topics.headline: tight passive sound
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The acoustic note does not add a separate lexical payoff after the retained passive-restraint topic.
topics.reason: The acoustic note does not add a separate lexical payoff after the retained passive-restraint topic.

words.gloss_range: subordinating particle that makes the worship act the governed content of prohibition
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) turns the next verb into the exact content of the prohibition. The worship remains a projected verbal act under governance, not a completed event or a detached noun, and the repeated complementizer later lets the reader compare the prohibited worship-clause with the commanded submission-clause.

topics.headline: worship packaged as complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prohibition targets a governed possible act, not a free-standing clause.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence shows the particle governing the following subjunctive verb as the complement of the passive prohibition.

topics.headline: first complementizer anticipates the second
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears forbidden worship and commanded submission as syntactic counterparts.
topics.reason: The same complementizer form recurs at word 18 and balances the two governed verbs.

words.gloss_range: barred first-person worship or service as a prospective act directed toward invoked others
words.root_gloss_range: worship, servitude, mastered service, and obedient dependency
words.prose: {{ar:أَعْبُدَ}} ({{tr:aʿbuda}}) is the worship-act placed under prohibition: a first-person possible service intercepted before it is performed. The root field keeps worship tied to mastered obedience and embodied dependency, so the barred act is more than ritual gesture. Locally, the direct object is the relative group that the audience invokes, making the act a rejected dependency mode rather than generic devotion. Created worship-purpose in 51:56 and the emptied false invocation of 40:74 sharpen the direction problem, while the worship-boundary formulas of 109:2-5 show the same family of refusal.

topics.headline: prospective worship held under prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speaker is barred from a possible act before it becomes performed service.
topics.reason: The particle before it governs the verb as subjunctive complement of the passive prohibition.

topics.headline: worship as mastered service
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels worship as service and dependent obedience, while local syntax keeps this as the barred act toward invoked others.
topics.reason: The root field supports worship and servitude; the local frame narrows it to the prohibited first-person act.

topics.headline: created worship purpose and false direction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare created worship purpose in 51:56 and the surah contrast with invoked objects in 40:74 to the local refusal.
topics.reason: The cited rows connect worship purpose and misdirected worship with concrete references, including 51:56 and 40:74.

topics.headline: barred worship contrasts commanded surrender
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah contrasts two dependency modes: service toward invoked others and surrender to the Lord.
topics.reason: The local discourse pairs this verb with the later submission verb.

topics.reason: The initial-sound echo is minor and does not add a separate reader-facing payoff beyond the retained verb opposition.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine plural relative head identifying the objects of barred worship through the audience’s action
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) does not name the rivals directly; it makes them a known class defined by the relative clause that follows. The masculine plural treats the invoked objects as addressable “those,” exposing the agency the audience grants them. The worship object is therefore built through the audience’s own calling practice, which both identifies and demotes the group without granting it an independent divine title.

topics.headline: relative head anchors object and clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the object of barred worship is identified through a clause, not by an honored name.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the relative pronoun the object of the worship verb and the head of the following relative clause.

topics.headline: definite plural class defined by action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the rivals as a known invoked class produced by the audience’s own practice.
topics.reason: The relative form and its clause make the referent definite and audience-defined.

words.gloss_range: ongoing plural audience invocation or appeal that defines the rival objects
words.root_gloss_range: calling, summoning, invoking, claiming, and appeal
words.prose: {{ar:تَدْعُونَ}} ({{tr:tadʿūna}}) brings the audience’s repeated practice inside the object clause: the rivals are those you keep calling. The root field adds request and claim pressure to the act of address, while the direct Form I verb keeps the calling simple and immediate. With the following exclusion phrase, the practice is indicted as address below God; the prohibition of calling with God in 72:18 and the surah reversal in 40:42 make that misdirection concrete. The wrong calling is answered by the command to surrender.

topics.headline: plural imperfect exposes current practice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rival objects are defined by the audience’s ongoing calls.
topics.reason: QAC identifies an imperfect second-person plural verb in the relative clause.

topics.headline: calling as appeal and claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears invocation as address, request, and claim, while the local phrase keeps it as the audience’s calling of rivals.
topics.reason: The root field supports calling and invocation; local syntax narrows it to the relative-clause practice.

topics.headline: calling with God becomes local boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect the local rejection to the prohibition of calling with God in 72:18 and the surah contrast in 40:42.
topics.reason: The cited rows give concrete references for the broader calling polemic.

topics.headline: relative clause demotes the rivals
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rivals are defined by the audience’s calling and then lowered by the exclusion phrase.
topics.reason: The following prepositional phrase supplies the indictment that completes the relative clause.

words.gloss_range: first preposition in an exclusion idiom marking separation from God
words.prose: {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) begins the exclusion phrase, shifting the audience’s invocation away from God rather than toward a legitimate source. Its separate particle form keeps the exclusion visible, and its contrast with the later source preposition makes the ayah’s movement sharp: one preposition separates false devotion; the other authenticates the proofs.

topics.headline: preposition begins the exclusion construction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the turn from calling to exclusion as soon as the preposition appears.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats the phrase that begins here as the complement to the calling verb.

topics.headline: separation preposition contrasts source preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same particle form first excludes rival devotion and later marks true proof-provenance.
topics.reason: The ayah uses the same surface particle in two opposed local functions.

topics.headline: sound binding into the next word
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The sound observation adds no distinct payoff beyond the visible exclusion construction.
topics.reason: The sound observation adds no distinct payoff beyond the visible exclusion construction.

words.gloss_range: construct noun in the idiom “besides/below,” marking rival objects as excluded beneath God
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, lowness, lesser status, and besides-language; submission-like pressure is only background when disputed
words.prose: {{ar:دُونِ}} ({{tr:dūni}}) is the hinge of demotion: the called rivals are not merely other addresses but are placed besides and below God. The construct binds the exclusion to God as its reference point. Protector-language in 39:3 shows the same besides-God demotion in another register. The lowness field survives as theological pressure, while local grammar keeps the phrase as the fixed exclusion construction rather than an independent doctrine of every related root branch.

topics.headline: construct phrase takes God as reference
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that exclusion is measured against God as the completing reference point.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies this noun as construct head completed by the divine name.

topics.headline: besides carries lowness pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the rivals as both other-than and lower-than, while the local idiom remains the selected phrase.
topics.reason: The root and related forms support lowness pressure; local grammar narrows it to the exclusion idiom.

topics.headline: protectors and worship below God
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect this demotion to protector-language in 39:3 and to the local worship/calling polemic.
topics.reason: The cited rows include 39:3 and strong co-occurrence with God and worship roots.

topics.headline: audience invocation is immediately lowered
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the audience’s calling is corrected by a demoting prepositional phrase.
topics.reason: The discourse rows tie this phrase to the calling verb and the ayah’s object inversion.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as the genitive endpoint of exclusion and the named center of worship-worthiness
words.root_gloss_range: deity, God, worship-worthiness, and awe or devotion pressure where derivationally relevant
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāh}}) anchors the exclusion phrase with the proper divine name, not a generic member of a deity class. That makes the phrase polemically precise: the invoked others are defined as below God, enacting the oneness pressure heard in 112:1. Derivational worship-worthiness pressure may sharpen the contrast, but the local word remains the proper name that later leads into the two lordship titles.

topics.headline: proper name anchors the exclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that exclusion is measured against the named God, not against an abstract deity category.
topics.reason: The word is the genitive complement completing the exclusion construction, and QAC marks it as a proper noun.

topics.headline: derivational pressure sharpens worthiness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels worship-worthiness in the background, while the local surface stays the proper divine name.
topics.reason: The derivational rows can intensify the contrast but do not replace the local proper-name reading.

topics.headline: named God as center of exclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect the enacted exclusion here with the oneness declaration in 112:1.
topics.reason: The cited rows include 112:1 and local worship-besides co-occurrence.

topics.headline: proper name leads into proof and lordship titles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sequence from God as exclusion endpoint to Lord as proof-source and surrender-target.
topics.reason: The discourse rows trace the divine reference chain through the ayah.

words.gloss_range: temporal threshold with causal warrant force introducing the proof-arrival clause
words.prose: {{ar:لَمَّا}} ({{tr:lammā}}) pivots from the barred worship to the arrival of proofs. It marks the completed arrival as the threshold that warrants the prohibition, so the refusal is not arbitrary; it follows when clear evidence has come. The particle’s timing and explanatory force stay joined in this local clause.

topics.headline: arrival becomes the warrant threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prohibition is tied to the moment proofs arrived, not to unexplained preference.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence links the following arrival clause as the explanation or occasion for the prohibition.

topics.headline: negative clause turns toward warrant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah moving from rejected worship into evidentiary grounding.
topics.reason: The particle introduces the proof-arrival clause after the exclusion phrase.

words.gloss_range: completed arrival of proofs to the speaker, with the speaker marked as recipient
words.root_gloss_range: coming, arriving, reaching, and event-like encounter
words.prose: {{ar:جَآءَنِىَ}} ({{tr:jāʾaniya}}) makes the proofs arrive to the speaker as an event, not as an abstract possession. The attached object suffix marks him as recipient, while the following subject shows what arrived. The arrival field gives the evidence encounter-weight, and the truth-arrival pattern of 17:81 gives a concrete parallel for arrival as decisive warrant. The perfect form closes the warrant before the later command. Reported final-yāʾ variation affects cadence or coloring, not the local recipient relation.

topics.headline: arrival event with speaker as recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices proofs coming to the speaker, not merely being known in general.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence show a perfect verb with an attached first-person object and a following subject.

topics.headline: proofs arrive as encounter
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the proofs as an arriving encounter, while local grammar keeps the selected sense as coming to the speaker.
topics.reason: The root field supports arrival-event pressure within the local proof clause.

topics.headline: truth-arrival pattern informs proof-arrival
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the proof-arrival warrant beside the truth-arrival pattern in 17:81.
topics.reason: The cited rows include 17:81 as a concrete arrival parallel.

topics.headline: verb before subject foregrounds the event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices arrival before the proofs are named, making the coming itself prominent.
topics.reason: The local word order places the verb before its postposed subject.

topics.headline: final-yāʾ variation affects cadence not parse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can register recitational coloring while keeping the same local reference and recipient relation.
topics.reason: Variant and prosodic rows affect cadence, not the attachment relation.

words.gloss_range: recognized multiple clear proofs as the postposed subject of arrival
words.root_gloss_range: clarity, distinction, separation, disclosure, and evidentiary making-clear
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتُ}} ({{tr:al-bayyinātu}}) names what arrived: recognized proofs that make the worship boundary clear. The plural accumulates evidentiary instances, while the root’s separation-field makes clarity a dividing act: it distinguishes true devotion from rival invocation. God’s clarifying of limits in 2:187 and the surah proof-polemics in 40:22 and 40:28 keep that evidentiary force concrete. Together with the threshold particle and arrival verb, the word grounds the refusal in received evidence from the Lord.

topics.headline: definite plural proofs as arriving subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the arriving warrant is a recognized set of proofs, not vague inspiration.
topics.reason: The noun is definite, plural, nominative, and the subject of the preceding arrival verb.

topics.headline: clarity divides and distinguishes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels proof as clarifying separation, while the local noun remains the concrete proofs that arrived.
topics.reason: The root field supports making clear through distinction; local grammar selects the proof noun.

topics.headline: proofs clarify boundaries
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can relate this proof-language to God clarifying limits in 2:187 and to the surah proof-polemics in 40:22 and 40:28.
topics.reason: The cited rows give concrete references for proof and clarification patterns.

topics.headline: proofs complete the threshold clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the threshold clause becoming a full warrant: when proofs arrived from the Lord.
topics.reason: The discourse rows bind threshold, arrival, proofs, and source into one warrant architecture.

words.gloss_range: source preposition marking the provenance of the proofs
words.prose: {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) marks provenance rather than exclusion: the proofs come from the speaker’s Lord. Its repetition after the earlier exclusion preposition sharpens the ayah’s contrast: rival devotion is away from God, while the warrant for refusal comes from the Lord.

topics.headline: source phrase authenticates proofs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proofs have a named provenance, not an anonymous evidentiary status.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence links this preposition to the proof-source phrase.

topics.headline: second preposition reverses the first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same particle form carrying the opposite local function: exclusion first, source now.
topics.reason: The repeated surface form contrasts local syntactic functions.

topics.headline: current source grounds prior rejection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices divine provenance continuing the reference chain that justified the refusal.
topics.reason: Boundary rows tie the proof-source phrase to the preceding rejection.

words.gloss_range: the speaker’s Lord as personal source of the proofs
words.root_gloss_range: lordship as owning, nurturing, sustaining, governing, and forming dependents
words.prose: {{ar:رَّبِّى}} ({{tr:rabbī}}) makes the proof-source relational and personal: the proofs come from the speaker’s Lord. The title carries care and authority together, so the warrant is neither private intuition nor arbitrary power. Against the wider Lord-of-worlds formula known from 1:2, this personal source later expands into the universal surrender-target, moving from “my Lord” to the Lord of the worlds.

topics.headline: first-person lordship sources the proofs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proofs are personally received from the speaker’s Lord.
topics.reason: The preposition governs this suffixed noun as the source complement.

topics.headline: lordship as care and rule
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels proof-giving as sustaining governance, while local grammar keeps the word as the speaker’s Lord.
topics.reason: The root field supports nurturing and authority pressure in the local title.

topics.headline: personal Lord participates in universal formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the personal title against the wider Lord-of-worlds formula known from 1:2.
topics.reason: The cited rows connect this title to the universal formula in 1:2.

topics.headline: source lordship precedes target lordship
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices personal evidence becoming cosmological allegiance by the end of the ayah.
topics.reason: The repeated root moves from proof-source to surrender-target across the ayah.

words.gloss_range: coordinating hinge from prohibited worship to commanded submission
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the hinge that refuses to leave the ayah at prohibition. It coordinates a second passive mandate with the first, so restraint opens into positive commission. The earlier below-God endpoint and the later Lord-ward endpoint are distributed across the two mandates. The small segmented conjunction keeps the turn visible before the command verb.

topics.headline: conjunction joins the second passive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah continues from blocked worship into commanded submission.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies this conjunction as coordinating the second passive clause.

topics.headline: refusal becomes commission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the clause hinge that completes the norm rather than stopping at refusal.
topics.reason: The discourse rows make the conjunction the transition from negative to positive mandate.

topics.reason: The recitational fusion note adds no separate payoff beyond the retained coordination hinge.

words.gloss_range: completed passive command imposed on the speaker as positive commission
words.root_gloss_range: command, order, affair, governance, and obligation
words.prose: {{ar:أُمِرْتُ}} ({{tr:umirtu}}) answers the earlier passive prohibition with a positive commission. The passive again foregrounds the speaker as recipient while veiling the commander, so the declaration is governed by received authority on both sides. The command-field makes the next act obligation, not preference, echoing the command-and-avoid polarity of 16:36 in first-person passive form. The paired passive form completes the prohibition-command architecture.

topics.headline: settled passive commission
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that surrender is commanded as an already imposed commission, not volunteered as a mood.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a perfect passive first-person verb coordinated with the earlier passive prohibition.

topics.headline: command as governing obligation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels command as governance and obligation, while local grammar keeps the selected sense as being commanded.

topics.headline: positive command answers avoidance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can compare the command to worship God and avoid false objects in 16:36 with this first-person passive report.
topics.reason: The cited rows include 16:36 as a concrete polarity parallel.

topics.headline: command completes the legal pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a full norm: false worship is blocked and surrender is required.
topics.reason: The discourse rows pair this passive command with the earlier passive prohibition.

words.gloss_range: second complementizer making submission the governed content of command
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) makes the following submission verb the content of the command rather than an independent description of current state. Because the same particle introduced the prohibited worship-act, the reader can see the two governed acts lined up: one barred, one required.

topics.headline: submission packaged as command complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that submission is required as command-content, not merely reported as biography.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence shows this particle governing the following subjunctive as complement of the passive command.

topics.headline: second complementizer completes the pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the forbidden worship-clause and commanded submission-clause as parallel alternatives.
topics.reason: The repeated complementizer aligns the two governed acts.

words.gloss_range: commanded first-person surrender directed by a prepositional complement toward lordship
words.root_gloss_range: yielding, surrender, handing over, safety, peace, and wholeness
words.prose: {{ar:أُسْلِمَ}} ({{tr:uslima}}) is the required positive act: first-person surrender directed to the Lord, not an abstract state or a possessed object. Form IV gives it active self-handover force, while the root field keeps surrender linked with safety and wholeness rather than mere loss of agency. The directed surrender recalls the face-to-God formula in 2:112. The ayah therefore turns from barred service to invoked others into directed allegiance to the Lord-of-worlds title that received praise in 40:65 and is followed by creator evidence in 40:67.

topics.headline: surrender takes a target of allegiance

topics.headline: projected act under command

topics.headline: yielding enters sound relation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels submission as yielded self and sound relation, while local grammar keeps the selected act as commanded surrender.
topics.reason: The root family supports surrender, safety, and wholeness pressure within the local command.

topics.headline: orientation follows a known surrender formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can connect the directed surrender here with surrendering the face to God in 2:112.
topics.reason: The cited rows include 2:112 as a concrete formulaic parallel.

topics.headline: dependency mode shifts
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices both object and dependency mode change: service to invoked beings is barred, surrender to the Lord is required.
topics.reason: The discourse rows contrast this verb with the earlier worship verb.

topics.headline: nearby title and creation frame specify the target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the Lord-of-worlds title from 40:65 becomes surrender’s target and is immediately followed by creation evidence in 40:67.
topics.reason: Boundary rows link the target title to 40:65 and 40:67.

words.gloss_range: preposition directing submission toward the Lord as recipient, purpose, and allegiance
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) gives surrender its endpoint. The preposition binds direction and allegiance to the Lord-title, reversing the earlier misdirected address below God. Because it is proclitic, the direction of surrender is heard as attached to the title rather than postponed.

topics.headline: preposition supplies the target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that submission has a directed recipient and is not a vague spiritual state.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence shows the preposition governing the following Lord-title as complement of the surrender verb.

topics.headline: clitic fuses direction to Lord-title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears surrender’s direction as bound to the Lord-title.
topics.reason: The proclitic form attaches to the following noun in recitation and spelling.

topics.headline: positive endpoint counters misdirection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the reversal: wrong calling is below God, right surrender is to the Lord.
topics.reason: The discourse rows contrast this target marker with the earlier exclusion phrase.

words.gloss_range: construct head “Lord” defining the surrender target by universal dominion
words.root_gloss_range: lordship as owning, sustaining, nurturing, governing, and mastering dependents
words.prose: {{ar:رَبِّ}} ({{tr:rabbi}}) begins the final title and lets lordship appear before it expands over all worlds. As a construct head, it is defined by the following genitive, so the surrender target is universal lordship, not local patronage. The title is a recognizable formula made into the endpoint of command, and the cosmic answer about the Lord of the worlds in 26:23-24 gives a concrete parallel for lordship beyond local rivals. baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired passives `nuhitu ... an a'bud` and `umirtu ... an uslima`, together with the repeated `rabbi`.
baseline_models.mechanism: A negative gate removes humble obedience from every object short of God, while a positive command delivers the self into the sole Lord's rule and formative care.

activation_trace.role: Active restraint from an act supplies the negative gate on service.
Humble worship and obedience identify what is withdrawn from the rivals.
Otherness and lower rank define the rival field from which service is removed.
Binding request supplies the positive jurisdiction that answers the prohibition.
Delivery and relinquishment make submission a transfer of one's affair, not a bare label.
Repair, nurture, and completion give the receiving Lord an ongoing formative function.

changed_reading.before: The speaker rejects one ritual practice and adopts another.
changed_reading.after: The speaker announces an exclusive transfer of obedience and self-disposal away from every rival and into the formative governance of the Lord.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: `Lamma ja'atni al-bayyinat min rabbi` interrupts the prohibition-command pair as an arrival from the Lord.
baseline_models.mechanism: The proofs do not merely decorate a conclusion: their arrival makes what was obscured appear and cuts a discriminating boundary between subordinate objects and the Lord.

activation_trace.role: Arrival and obtaining turn evidence into an event that reaches the speaker.
Appearance and disclosure make the evidence perceptibly clear.
Separation gives that disclosure the functional role of cutting rival claims apart.
Nearness short of the goal locates the called objects on the deficient side of the new boundary.
Lordship, ownership, and sovereignty identify the source and far side of the distinction.

changed_reading.before: Clear proofs are reasons appended to an already settled refusal.
changed_reading.after: The arrival of disclosure itself creates the boundary that terminates rival service and makes exclusive submission possible.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The ayah begins with `qul`, describes what the addressees `tad'una`, and embeds a second command in `umirtu`.
baseline_models.mechanism: A commanded utterance answers the addressees' own speech-act of calling: public saying performs the speaker's changed allegiance rather than merely reporting an inward state.

activation_trace.role: Voiced speech makes the refusal an outwardly issued declaration.
Speech as creed lets the declaration expose the allegiance it enacts.
Calling and verbal inclination identify the rival summons that the declaration counters.
Obligating command frames both the announced submission and, through `qul`, its publication.

changed_reading.before: The sentence privately states the speaker's religious position.
changed_reading.after: The sentence is a commissioned counter-speech that publicly breaks the addressees' summons and performs a new allegiance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The reciprocal calls of 40:41-43 are vectors with opposed destinations: one call separates into rescue, the other recruits into fire, while every trajectory returns to God. This makes accepting a call function as allegiance and therefore as worship.

activation_trace.role: Verbal calling anchors the focus phrase as a summons capable of inclining its hearer.
Humble obedience supplies the allegiance enacted when a summons is accepted.
Two reciprocal verbal inclinations are explicitly aimed toward opposite destinations.
Rescue as separation gives the counter-summons a concrete destination away from entrapment.
The repeated reciprocal call identifies the rival invitation with disbelief and association.
Return to God supplies the terminal direction against which both summonses are tested.

structural_cues: 40:41 balances `I call you` against `you call me` and names rescue and fire as destinations.
40:42 repeats the reversal and spells out the demanded disbelief and association.
40:43 closes the exchange with the rivals' ineffective call and the common return to God.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies reciprocal summonses, stated destinations, and final return; I infer that yielding to a summons installs an allegiance expressed as worship. A live alternative keeps these as invitations without making them a full account of cultic service.

changed_reading.before: `Those whom you call` names objects addressed in prayer.
changed_reading.after: `Those whom you call` also names a recruitment system: their summons asks the speaker to enter a destination-bearing allegiance, which the focus declaration refuses.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah joins invocation to two tests: can the called power issue an effective judgment, and can it answer? God judges and answers; the rivals judge nothing, and refusal to call the Lord is named pride against worship.

activation_trace.role: Calling supplies the focus's request-and-allegiance interface.
Decisive judgment is contrasted between God and the called rivals, making efficacy a jurisdictional test.
The same verbal invocation is attached to powers that cannot decide anything.
Otherness from God marks the failed jurisdiction as the exact rival field repeated in the focus.
The Lord's invitation to call establishes the valid side of the response relation.
Answering speech completes the call-response circuit that rival powers leave open.
Worship and humble obedience are explicitly paired with the command to call, joining petition to service.

structural_cues: 40:20 closely anticipates the focus phrase `those they call apart from Him` and denies those objects any judgment.
40:60 places `call Me, I will answer you` beside pride against `My worship`.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies failed rival judgment and a divine call-answer-worship sequence; I infer that worship includes where one directs dependence and recognizes effective jurisdiction. A live alternative treats judgment, petition, and worship as adjacent but distinct arguments.

changed_reading.before: The prohibition concerns misdirected ritual devotion.
changed_reading.after: The prohibition extracts dependence from nonanswering, nonjudging authorities and relocates petition, obedience, and jurisdiction together under the Lord.

context_deltas.mechanism: The believer in Pharaoh's house moves from concealed faith to speech when a man may be killed for saying `my Lord is God` after bringing clear proofs. The focus's matching cluster of saying, Lord, arrival, and proofs becomes costly public testimony against coercive rule.

activation_trace.role: Voiced declaration anchors the focus as an act performed before hearers.
Manifest proof anchors the reason the declaration can no longer remain inward.
Speech moves from narration to the incriminating confession `my Lord is God`.
Concealment supplies the pressured prior state from which public testimony emerges.
Taking life supplies the coercive cost attached to naming the true Lord.
Disclosed proofs reproduce the focus's evidentiary trigger inside the threatened testimony.
Truthful speech supplies the live alternative to the regime's accusation of lying.

structural_cues: 40:25 answers the arrival of truth with a command to kill.
40:28 repeats the focus cluster: saying, `my Lord`, arrival, and clear proofs.
The believing speaker is introduced as concealing faith before he speaks.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a close lexical echo inside a scene of concealment and threatened killing; I infer that the focus utterance belongs to the same genre of risk-bearing counter-testimony. A live alternative treats the echo as thematic support without transferring the narrative danger to this speaker.

changed_reading.after: `Say` commissions evidence-responsive resistance: the speaker publicly withdraws service from rival power even where naming the Lord can carry a coercive cost.

context_deltas.mechanism: The believing speaker entrusts his `amr` to God and is then protected. That sequence activates `uslima` as a deliberate delivery of one's affair to the Lord, not as inert capitulation.

activation_trace.role: Binding command supplies the focus's initiating authority.
Delivery and relinquishment supply the act by which the commanded self is handed over.
Entrusting a matter to another gives submission the active mechanism of delegated reliance.
One's affair or condition is the object transferred, creating a live play against the focus's being commanded.
Protective warding supplies the narrated consequence of entrusted reliance.

structural_cues: 40:44 joins public speech to `I entrust my affair to God`.
40:45 immediately narrates protection from the plotted harms.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit entrustment of an affair followed by protection; I infer that this gives functional texture to the focus's `uslima`. A live alternative lets `aslama` emphasize obedience while treating entrustment as only one neighboring posture.

changed_reading.before: Submission is passive compliance with a superior order.
changed_reading.after: Submission is an active transfer of one's exposed affair to the Lord, allowing public obedience without pretending to control its outcome.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate lead-in fills `Lord` with operations: arranging rest, creating every thing, stabilizing earth, forming bodies, and allotting provision. Submission to the Lord of the worlds therefore aligns the self with the source that continually houses, forms, and sustains it.

activation_trace.role: Repair, nurture, and completion anchor lordship as formative care.
Wholeness and freedom from harm supply the fitting state under sustaining lordship.
Restful familiarity makes the ordered night a habitable provision.
Creative origination extends the Lord's formative reach to every thing.
Fixity and settlement make the earth an enabling base rather than inert scenery.
Form and fashioned configuration place the worshipper's own body inside lordly formation.
Allotted giving supplies the material continuation of the formed life.
Repeated formative lordship explicitly gathers habitat, body, and provision under `Lord of the worlds`.

structural_cues: 40:61-64 proceeds from temporal habitat to universal creation, terrestrial settlement, bodily form, and provision.
40:64 closes that material sequence with the same `Lord of the worlds` phrase used in the focus.
40:65 repeats `Lord of the worlds` immediately before 40:66.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a chain of sustaining operations closed by the focus title; I infer that these operations are the practical content of `rabb` to which the self submits. A live alternative treats them as proofs of sovereignty without making formation central to submission.

changed_reading.before: `Lord of the worlds` is chiefly a universal sovereignty title.
changed_reading.after: The title names the one whose rule is experienced as habitat, formation, and provision, so submission is creaturely alignment with sustaining care.

context_deltas.mechanism: A later forced reckoning repeats `apart from God` and `we used to call`, but the objects first go missing and are then denied the status of anything called at all. The focus declaration becomes the same truth spoken voluntarily before exposure makes denial unavoidable.

activation_trace.role: Otherness from God anchors the rival domain named in both present declaration and later reckoning.
Calling anchors the action that the focus renounces before its objects collapse.
The exact rival relation reappears under retrospective questioning.
Loss of the object makes the formerly called powers unavailable at the point of reckoning.
Retrospective calling repeats the focus action in a confession that tries to erase it.
A knowable, reportable thing supplies the status denied to the vanished rivals.

structural_cues: 40:74 repeats the focus construction `apart from God` plus the root for calling.
The answer moves from `they are lost from us` to `we did not call anything before`.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exact lexical recurrence and a two-step collapse from absence to denial; I infer a temporal contrast between voluntary truth now and compelled recognition later. A live alternative reads 40:74 only as confirmation of the rivals' failure, without treating 40:66 as an anticipatory confession.

changed_reading.before: The speaker simply denies present participation in rival worship.
changed_reading.after: The speaker gives early and freely the truthful confession that rival callers will reach only after their objects vanish: nothing apart from God merits being called or served.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing sequence contrasts two `lamma` thresholds. Messengers' proofs arrive while response remains possible, but inherited knowledge is preferred; only when force is seen does exclusive belief appear, and then it no longer benefits. The focus's response when proofs arrive is therefore timely surrender before compelled sight.

activation_trace.role: Arrival anchors the first threshold at which the speaker changes allegiance.
Disclosed proof identifies what is visible enough for a free response without coercive sight.
The same arrival opens the comparison with communities who respond differently.
The same manifest proofs make refusal a response to disclosure rather than lack of evidence.
Exultant self-satisfaction supplies the mechanism that closes the first response window.
Knowledge already possessed becomes the rival disclosure in which the rejecters take satisfaction.
Direct sight marks the later coercive threshold at which profession finally occurs.
Overpowering severity explains why the later profession is compelled rather than freely evidence-responsive.
Benefit opposed to harm supplies the explicit failure of belief adopted only after direct sight.
Repeated seeing closes the contrast with the focus's earlier reception of proofs.

structural_cues: 40:83 and 40:84 repeat `fa-lamma` across arrival of proofs and sight of force.
40:84 voices the exclusive belief and rejection of partners that 40:66 already declares.
40:85 states that belief after the second threshold no longer benefits.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated temporal constructions, matching exclusive profession, and the loss of benefit after sight; I infer that the timing of response is ethically decisive. A live alternative takes the focus's `lamma` as causal rather than as an opened response window.

changed_reading.before: `When the clear proofs came to me` only supplies the reason for the speaker's conclusion.
changed_reading.after: It marks the still-open moment in which disclosure can become free submission, before overwhelming sight makes the same exclusive confession too late to benefit.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the non-dominant د ع ع target behind focus `tad'una`, not the ordinary calling branch. It remains anchored by that packet-supplied split mapping and by the later bodily sequence of collars, linked chains, and dragging. Downstream prose should present it only as an exploratory material analogy for coercive recruitment, never as a replacement lexical translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus occurrence `tad'una` resolves not only to د ع و but also to the packet's split target د ع ع, whose first branch is violent pushing.

activation_trace.role: Violent pushing supplies a form-distant material image for how a rival summons can coerce movement.
A collar that binds an organ turns coerced allegiance into bodily restraint.
The neck locates the point where claimed guidance becomes imposed control.
Connected links supply the mechanism by which individual restraint becomes a continuous forced path.
Dragging and extension complete the image of a summons that moves its adherent by force.

changed_reading.before: The addressees neutrally call upon rival objects.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, their calling is also a coercive propulsion system: the refused allegiance promises direction but terminates in linked restraint and dragging.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it places the human command to submit beside the creative `Be`, risking a collapse of moral response into automatic creaturely occurrence. It remains anchored in the focus's paired command, saying, and surrender and in the immediately following staged creation and decisive command. Downstream prose should mark it as an analogy between ethical and ontological responsiveness, not an identity between them.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus joins `qul`, `umirtu`, and `uslima`; 40:67-68 then stages human formation and a divine affair completed by `He says to it: Be, and it is`.

activation_trace.role: Issued speech anchors the human declaration that will echo, without equaling, the later creative saying.
Binding command anchors submission as a morally addressed act.
Delivery of oneself supplies the ethical response compared with creaturely becoming.
Creative origination places the addressed human inside a prior history of received existence.
The clinging blood-stage supplies one concrete transition in the creature's involuntary formation.
Perfecting and carrying an act through gives the divine affair decisive efficacy.
Affair or case links the creative sequence back to the focus's command root without equating their senses.
Creative saying supplies the higher-order speech to which the focus's commanded saying can be analogically related.
Occurrence and presence enact immediate creaturely responsiveness to the creative word.

changed_reading.before: The speaker receives a discrete religious command late in an otherwise self-directed life.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, conscious submission is the ethical recognition of a condition already written through the creature's staged becoming: life has always been received under effective command.

strongest_changes: Calling became both reciprocal recruitment toward a destination and a test of answering jurisdiction, rather than prayer-language alone.
The focus declaration became public testimony in a coercive field through the close 40:28 echo of saying, Lord, arriving, and clear proofs.
Submission became active entrustment of one's affair and alignment with the Lord's sustaining formation.
The final repeated `lamma` sequence made arrival of proofs a timely response window before compelled sight.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah recurrence turned the focus into a junction: it answers the believing man's counter-summons, gathers the call-worship and call-response circuits, names the sustaining Lord described immediately before it, and speaks early the confession that failed callers reach only after their objects disappear.
remaining_uncertainties: The focus form `uslima` can carry obedience, relinquishment, and movement toward wholeness in different proportions.
The 40:28 lexical echo strongly re-voices the declaration, but the packet alone cannot decide whether the same degree of mortal danger should be transferred to 40:66.
The split د ع ع activation and the creative-command analogy are worth retaining only with their stated exploratory containment.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Clear evidence simultaneously restrains one direction and opens surrender in another.** `ن ه ي/B001` gives restraint from an act, `ب ي ن/B001` separation, and `س ل م/B001` soundness and safety. The paired passive commands follow evidentiary arrival. I infer that clarification separates rival paths strongly enough to block one and make whole alignment possible; surrender reads as restored soundness, not mere capitulation.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The creation sequence in 40:67 grounds surrender in embodied dependence; sound alignment responds to a life whose materials, stages, and term are received.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Restraint clears rival attachments so the self can be handed over.** Lexically, `ن ه ي:B001` is restraining from an act, `ع ب د:B003` worship and submissive obedience, and `س ل م:B012` handing over and letting go alongside `B001` soundness and safety. Structurally, exclusive invocation in 40:65 becomes a prohibition against serving invoked others and a command to submit; 40:67 then places the addressee inside a wholly given developmental process. Prohibition removes competing claims, while submission transfers the self to the stated Lord. The packet gives negative restraint and positive command; I infer that release from rival service enables whole handover. The ayah reads as a two-stage reallocation of allegiance rather than redundant negation and affirmation.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 40:71 supplies forced collars and chains, sharpening submission by contrast: `س ل م:B012` is a willing handover before evidence becomes an imposed binding.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı sesle ortaya çıkarılan söz ve harflerden kurulu sözlü ifade olarak verir. Geçici çerçeve aynı çekirdeği taşıyor; dil organı, hükümdar unvanı ve mecazi yan kullanımlar bu dalın dışında kalır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal çıplak söz söyleme ve söylenmiş söz çekirdeğidir; organ, unvan, söylenti ve mecazlar ayrı dallardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam bare olduğu için tanım çıplak söyleme ve sözlü ifade anlamıyla sınırlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir düşünceyi veya sözü sesli biçimde dışa vurma ve böyle dışa vurulmuş harfli sözlü ifade anlamıdır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek işlem, sözü sesli olarak dışa çıkarmaktır.
Söylenen şey tek söz, cümle, şiir veya konuşma ölçeğinde olabilir.
Ad biçimleri aynı söylenmiş söz alanında toplanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, sözü sesle dışa çıkarılan ve harflerden oluşan sözlü ifade çekirdeğinde toplar; ad biçimleri de aynı alana bağlıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sözü sesli biçimde ortaya koyma ve ortaya konmuş sözlü ifade için genel başlık olarak uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Sesle dışa vurma ve sözlü ifade çekirdeğini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Fiil bağlamında kişinin sözü sesli olarak ortaya koymasını karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Fiilsel söyleme işlemini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Ad bağlamında söylenmiş söz veya konuşma ürünü için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Söylenmiş ifade sonucunu korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal sözün sesle dışa vurulmasını ve söylenmiş ifadeyi anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal konuşmayı sağlayan organ olan dili adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de konuşma alanına bağlıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Okur karışıklığı söz ile onu üreten organ arasındadır. Bu dalda ürün ve eylem merkezdir; komşuda bedensel araç merkezdir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal hem söyleme eylemini hem de söylenmiş söz adlarını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal konuşmanın dille çıkarılıp lafza dönüşmesi üzerinde durur.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de sözün sesli hale gelmesini paylaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu daha doğrudan telaffuz olayına odaklanır; bu dalda söylenmiş sözün ad alanı da çekirdeğe dahildir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal bir sözün söylenmesini veya söylenmiş olmasını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal sözün insanlar arasında yayılıp söylentiye dönüşmesini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her ikisinde de söylenen söz bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dalda yayılma şart değildir; komşu dalda sözün dolaşıma girmesi anlamın asli sınırıdır.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه قال يقول قولا، والقول والقيل، والكلام المركب من الحروف إذا أبرز بالنطق، مفردا كان أو جملة أو قصيدة أو خطبة.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه اللسان نفسه، ولا لقب القيل الحميري، ولا الدلالة غير اللفظية إلا في فروعها الخاصة.
branches.source_phrase_ar: القول من النطق (maqayis)؛ قال يقول قولا وقولة ومقالا ومقالة (sihah)؛ القول والقيل واحد (mufradat)؛ المركب من الحروف المبرز بالنطق (mufradat)؛ القيل من القول اسم (ayn)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi ilgili biçimi doğrudan konuşma organı olan dil diye açıklar. Geçici çerçeve bu organ anlamını doğru taşır ve söylenmiş söz ya da söz sahibi anlamlarını bu dalın dışında bırakır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal organ adıdır; sözün kendisini, konuşma eylemini veya unvan sahibini kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam bare olduğu için tanım, tek biçimin çıplak organ anlamına bağlı kalır.

concept_map.definition: Söz söylemeye araç olan konuşma organı, yani dil anlamıdır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek anlam, konuşmayı sağlayan bedensel organdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar bu dalı konuşma organı olan dil anlamında ortaklaştırır; söz veya unvan anlamı eklenmez.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sözün kendisi değil, sözü çıkaran bedensel araç kastedildiğinde uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Organ anlamını ve konuşma işlevini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Organ adı olarak doğal çeviridir; bağlam konuşma eylemini değil organı göstermelidir.

error_profile.preserves: Türkçedeki organ adını korur.
error_profile.adds: Türkçede aynı kelime konuşulan sistem anlamını da çağırabilir.
error_profile.collision: Dil kelimesi dil sistemiyle karışabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal konuşmanın organını adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal sözü söyleme eylemini ve söylenmiş ifadeyi anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de konuşma ve söz alanında bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal araçtır; komşu dal bu araçla çıkan söz veya söyleme işlemidir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal tek özel biçimin söz organı anlamını verir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal organın genel adı, gücü, cinsiyeti ve çoğulları gibi daha geniş ad alanını taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de bedensel konuşma organını paylaşır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Anlam merkezleri örtüşür; komşu dal organ adının daha geniş sözlük ailesini kapsadığı için sınır tam değildir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal konuşma organının kendisini belirtir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal konuşamama veya konuşmanın tutulması durumunu belirtir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de konuşma yetisiyle ilgilidir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Organ adı ile konuşma yokluğu aynı alanı paylaşır, fakat birinin çekirdeği araç, diğerinin çekirdeği yoksunluktur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Aday komşular organ, konuşma bozukluğu, ses ve ana kök dalları açısından değerlendirildi; en doğrudan organ-karşıtlıkları yayımlandı.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه المقول بمعنى اللسان.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه القول المنطوق نفسه ولا صاحب القول.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kişiyi çok sözlü, güzel konuşan veya dili güçlü biri olarak niteleyen adları bir araya getirir. Bu, bir kez söyleme eylemi değil, kişide yerleşik konuşkanlık veya söz becerisi niteliğidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal kişi niteliğidir; tekil söyleme eylemi veya insanlar arasında yayılan söylenti değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam non_bare olduğu için tanım, kişi niteleyen özel biçimlerle sınırlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişiyi çok konuşan, dili güçlü veya söz söylemede atak olarak niteleyen kullanımdır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek anlam, kişide söz söyleme çokluğu veya söz becerisi niteliğidir.
Nitelik özellikle insan için kullanılır ve tek bir söyleme olayını göstermez.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar bu dalı kişiyi çok sözlü, dili güçlü veya konuşkan diye niteleyen biçimler etrafında ortaklaştırır.

error_profile.preserves: Kişi niteliğini ve söz çokluğunu korur.

error_profile.preserves: Söz çokluğu niteliğini korur.
error_profile.loses: Dilin güçlü veya etkili oluşu ayrıca söylenmeyebilir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Söz becerisi ve etkili konuşma yönü öne çıktığında uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Söz söyleme gücü niteliğini korur.
error_profile.loses: Sadece konuşma çokluğu yönünü ikinci plana iter.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de insanın dil ve söz gücü niteliğidir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi belirli bir eski bölgesel yönetici unvanını, çoğullarını, kadın biçimini ve sözü geçerli kişi açıklamasını birlikte verir. Geçici çerçeve, sıradan söz anlamı değil unvan ve otorite anlamı olduğunu doğru sınırlar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal unvan ve makam sahibidir; sıradan söylenmiş söz veya söylenti anlamı değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam bare olduğu için tanım bu adların çıplak unvan anlamını verir.

concept_map.definition: Sözü geçerli kabul edilen yerel hükümdar veya yönetici unvanı, onun çoğulları ve kadın için kullanılan biçimi anlamıdır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek anlam, sözü geçen yönetici veya hükümdar unvanıdır.
Dal çoğul adları ve kadın için kullanılan unvan biçimini de içerir.
Unvanın açıklaması, sözü yürüyen kişi fikrine bağlanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Aktarım, bölgesel bir yönetici unvanını ve çoğullarını sözü geçerli kişi açıklamasıyla birleştirir; sıradan söz anlamından ayrıdır.

source_note.MU: Tekil aktarım, bir şeye içten önem verme anlamındaki kalıp kullanımını verir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi düşünce bilimi bağlamında sözün bir şeyin tanımı veya sınır bildirimi için kullanıldığını açıklar. Bu, normal konuşma değil, teknik tanım işleviyle sınırlı bir kalıptır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam collocation olduğu için tanım, teknik tanım bildiren özel kalıplara bağlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Düşünce bilimi bağlamında bir şeyin ne olduğunu belirleyen tanım veya sınır bildirimi için söz kelimesinin kullanılmasıdır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek anlam, sözün bir şeyin tanımı veya sınırı olarak kullanılmasıdır.
Kullanım teknik düşünce bilimi bağlamıyla sınırlıdır.

branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه القول المنطوق العادي إلا إذا أريد به الحد.
branches.source_phrase_ar: يستعمله المنطقيون في معنى الحد فيقولون قول الجوهر كذا وقول العرض كذا أي حدهما (mufradat)

source_note.MU: Tekil aktarım, teknik bağlamda sözün bir şeyin tanımı anlamında kullanılmasını verir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi sesli bir hitap gelmeden anlamın kişinin içine doğmasını ve bunun söz diye adlandırılmasını anlatır. Çerçeve, işitilen konuşmadan ayrılan içe doğan anlam aktarımını doğru yakalar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal içe doğan anlam aktarımıdır; işitilen sözlü hitap değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam non_bare olduğu için tanım özel içe doğma bağlamıyla sınırlıdır.

concept_map.definition: İşitilen bir hitap olmadan, bir anlamın kişinin içine doğması ve bunun söz diye adlandırılmasıdır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek anlam, sözsüz biçimde içe doğan anlam aktarımıdır.
Bu kullanım işitilen hitabı özellikle dışarıda bırakır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kanıt bu özel dalı tek bir aktarım üzerinden verir; ortaklaştırılacak ayrı bir çok kaynaklı iddia yoktur.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal kişinin içinde bulunan fakat söylemediği sözdür.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İkisi de iç zihinsel söz veya anlam alanındadır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dalda anlam kişiye gelmiş sayılır; komşu dalda kişinin içinde tuttuğu ve henüz dışa vurmadığı söz vardır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Aday komşular iletim, çağrı, ses, beden eğilmesi ve kökün iç söz dalları açısından tarandı; sessiz iç anlam sınırı yayımlandı.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه القول في الإلهام، حيث يسمى إلقاء المعنى قولا من غير خطاب وارد.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه الخطاب اللفظي المسموع.
branches.source_phrase_ar: في الإلهام فإن ذلك لم يكن بخطاب ورد عليه بل كان ذلك إلهاما فسماه قولا (mufradat)

root_profile.summary: Bu kök, sesle söze dökme çekirdeğinden konuşma organı, konuşkan kişi, eski unvan, yalan isnat, söylenti, müzakere, hüküm dayatma, iç söz, görüş benimseme, sözsüz belirtme, içten önemseme, teknik tanım ve içe doğan anlam gibi ayrı dallara yayılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi azlığı çokluğun karşıtı olarak verir; ayrıca yoksulluk, düşüklük, bir şeyi az görme ve belirli yapılarda yokluğa ya da seyrekliğe yaklaşan kullanımları açıkça destekler.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol yalnızca sayı ve miktar azlığını ve buna bağlı kullanımları kapsar; yükseklik, kap, taşıma ve titreme anlamlarını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Temel azlık anlamı ile yoksullaşma ve az görme gibi türemiş biçimler birlikte bulunur; yokluk ve seyrekleşme anlamları ise yalnızca belirtilen yapılara bağlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin sayı, miktar ya da ölçü bakımından çok olmayışını bildirir. Bundan yoksulluk ve düşüklük, bir şeyi az sayma veya az gösterme ve belirli yapılarda hiçlik ya da seyrek gerçekleşme anlamları gelişir.

facets.statement: Bir varlığın sayı, miktar veya ölçü bakımından çok olmayışıdır.
Azlık, kişinin yoksullaşması veya toplum içinde düşük ve değersiz görülmesi sonucuna uzanabilir.
Bir şeyi gerçekte ya da değerlendiren kişinin gözünde az sayma ve az gösterme anlamını taşır.
Belirli olumsuzluk ve sıklık yapılarında hiç yokluğu veya bir eylemin pek seyrek gerçekleşmesini anlatır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar azlığın temel sayı ve miktar karşıtlığında birleşir; yoksulluk ve düşüklük, az sayma ve bazı yapılarda yokluğa yaklaşan kullanım bu çekirdeğin düzenli uzantılarıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sayı, miktar veya ölçünün çok olmayışını bildiren temel anlam için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Çokluğun karşıtı olan sayı ve miktar azlığını doğrudan korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir şeyin sayı veya miktar bakımından çok olmadığının söylendiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Temel azlık durumunu doğal bir Türkçe yapıyla tam olarak verir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Azlığın kişide yoksulluk ve toplumsal düşüklük sonucu doğurduğu bağlamlara özgüdür.

error_profile.preserves: Yoksulluk ile düşüklük arasındaki kaynakta kurulan uzantıyı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir miktarın veya verilen bir şeyin yetersiz ya da küçük sayıldığı değerlendirme bağlamlarında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Değerlendiren kişinin bir şeyi az sayması anlamını tam olarak korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yalnızca sıklığı çok düşüren veya olumsuzluğu pekiştiren kalıplaşmış yapılarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kalıba bağlı seyrekleşme ve yokluğa yaklaşma değerlerini korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol azlığı yoksulluk, düşüklük, az sayma ve kalıba bağlı yokluk değerlerine kadar genişletir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol genel azlığı özellikle mal, yiyecek ve verili miktar örnekleri çevresinde toplar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki kol da bir şeyin sayı veya miktar bakımından çok olmayışını anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Temel azlık alanları büyük ölçüde örtüşür; ancak bu kolun değerlendirme, toplumsal sonuç ve kalıba bağlı olumsuzluk uzantıları komşu kartta aynı sınırla kurulmaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kolun çekirdeği sayı ve miktar azlığıdır; değersizlik bunun ikincil bir sonucudur.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kolun çekirdeği güçsüzlük, aşağılık ve düşünme yetisindeki zayıflıktır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki kol da azlıkla değersizlik veya düşüklük arasında anlam ilişkisi kurabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu kolda değersizlik azlığın uzantısıdır; komşu kolda ise zayıflık ve aşağılık bağımsız çekirdektir, bu yüzden olağan kullanımda birbirlerinin yerine geçmezler.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol bir şeyin sayıca veya miktarca az oluşunu bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol bir şeyin başını, tepesini veya en üst bölümünü bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Aynı kökün sesçe yakın iki ayrı anlam kolu olmaları dışında ortak çekirdekleri yoktur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Ses benzerliği anlam birliği doğurmaz: biri çokluğun karşıtı olan azlığı, diğeri uzamsal olarak en üstte bulunan baş veya tepeyi adlandırır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı; genel azlıkla en yakın örtüşme, değersizlikle kurulan yan ilişki ve aynı kökteki tepe anlamıyla olası karışma en açıklayıcı üç sınır olarak seçildi.
branches.what_is_ar: القليل والقِلَّة ضد الكثرة، ويدخل فيه الافتقار والذلة، وتقليل الشيء في العين، واستقلاله، واستعمال القليل للنفي أو للندرة
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس علو الشيء ولا الجرة ولا الحمل ولا الرعدة
branches.source_phrase_ar: القل القليل؛ رماه الله بالقل والذل أي بالقلة والذلة (jamhara)؛ شيء قليل وجمعه قلل؛ قل الشيء يقل قلة؛ قلله في عينه؛ أقل افتقر؛ استقله عده قليلا (sihah)؛ قل الشيء يقل قلة فهو قليل وقلال؛ القل من الرجال الخسيس الدنيء؛ قليلة ولا كثيرة؛ قليلا ما يؤمنون؛ قاللت لفلان؛ تقاللت ما أعطاني (tahdhib)؛ القلة والكثرة يستعملان في الأعداد؛ يكنى بالقلة عن الذلة؛ يكنى بها تارة عن العزة؛ قليل يعبر به عن النفي (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyin en üstünü veya başını çekirdek anlam olarak verir; dağın yuvarlak üst bölümü, insan başı ve kılıcın başındaki topuz bu çekirdeğin açık uzmanlaşmalarıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol uzamsal başı ve en üst parçayı bildirir; sayısal azlık ya da büyük kap anlamını içermez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel baş ve en üst bölüm anlamı ile dağ tepesi, insan başı ve kılıç topuzu gibi yapıya bağlı uzmanlaşmalar ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin başını veya en üst bölümünü bildirir. Dağın üstteki yuvarlak parçası, insan başı ve kılıcın sap ucundaki topuz bu uzamsal çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir nesnenin veya oluşumun başı ya da en üstte bulunan bölümüdür.
Dağın en üstünde yer alan, kimi tanımda yuvarlak biçimli bölümünü adlandırır.
İnsan başı ile kılıcın sap ucundaki başlık veya topuz da aynı üst ve baş kavramıyla adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir şeyin başı ve en üst bölümü üzerinde birleşir; dağ tepesi temel örnektir, insan başı ile kılıç topuzu da aynı biçimsel ve uzamsal çizgide yer alır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir nesnenin ya da doğal oluşumun en üst bölümünü ve başını kapsayan genel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Baş olma ile uzamsal olarak en üstte bulunma çekirdeğini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Dağın en üst ve kimi zaman yuvarlak bölümünün adlandırıldığı bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Dağa özgü en üst bölüm uzmanlaşmasını doğrudan korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İnsan başının veya başka bir şeyin baş sayılan üst bölümünün kastedildiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Üst bölümün baş olarak kavranmasını kısa ve doğal biçimde verir.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kılıcın sap ucunda bulunan başlık ya da topuz parçası anlatılırken kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kılıca özgü baş veya üst parça uzmanlaşmasını korur.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol başla ilgili renk, büyüklük, yaralanma, sayım ve alışveriş kullanımlarına kadar uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki kol da insanın veya başka bir şeyin başını ve en üst bölümünü adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Baş ve üst bölüm çekirdekleri yakındır; bu kol tepe ve topuz biçimini öne çıkarırken komşu kol başı daha geniş varlık ve kullanım alanlarında işler.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol insan başını ve kılıç topuzunu da üst veya baş kavramına bağlar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol yüksekliği hörgüç, soy üstünlüğü ve toplumsal onur alanlarına genişletir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki kol da bir şeyin en yüksek, öne çıkan tepe bölümünü anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu kol somut baş ve üst parça sınırında kalır; komşu kol fiziksel doruktan toplumsal yüceliğe uzanan daha geniş bir yükseklik alanı kurar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu kol başı, tepeyi ve en üstte bulunan parçayı bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu kol sayı, miktar veya ölçü bakımından azlığı bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Aynı kökün sesçe yakın iki ayrı anlam kolu olmaları dışında ortak çekirdekleri yoktur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu anlam uzamsal bir üst bölüm adıdır; komşu anlam ise çokluğun karşıtı olan nicelik durumudur.

branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس القلة بمعنى الصغر أو العدد القليل، وليس إناء القُلَّة

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi büyük bir küp veya iri kap anlamında birleşir; iki kaplık ölçü ve belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler de aynı kap anlamını somutlaştırır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol büyük bir kap türünü ve onun ölçü değerini kapsar; nicelik azlığı veya dağ tepesi anlamını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Büyük küp anlamı çekirdektir; belirli bir bölgeye bağlanan kap adı ile iki kaplık ölçü yalnızca kendi yapılardaki uzmanlaşmalardır.

concept_map.definition: Büyük bir küpü veya küpe benzeyen iri kabı bildirir. Belirli bir bölgenin iri küpleri ve iki böyle kabın aldığı miktar bu kap anlamına bağlı özel kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Küpe benzeyen, özellikle sıvı taşımaya veya saklamaya elverişli büyük bir kaptır.
Belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler veya büyük toprak kaplar bu adın tanınmış bir türünü oluşturur.
İki büyük kap, bu iki kabın kendisini veya onların aldığı sıvı miktarını bildiren bir ölçü değeri kazanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar iri bir küp veya büyük kap üzerinde birleşir; tanınmış bölgesel kaplar büyüklüğü örnekler, iki kaplık kullanım ise nesne adını kapasite ölçüsüne taşır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Küpe benzeyen iri kabı adlandıran temel ve en doğal Türkçe karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Kabın küp türünde ve olağandan büyük oluşunu birlikte korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yükü taşıma veya taşıyabilme ile öznenin yükselip harekete geçmesini aynı kolda açıkça toplar; kuşun uçuşa kalkması, göğün yükselmesi ve yolcuların yüklenip ayrılması ayrı katılımcı gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Taşıma, yükselme ve yüklenerek yola koyulma bu kolun sınırıdır; salt sayısal azlık bu anlamlara katılmaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yük taşıma ile yükselme çekirdek çizgileri ayrılır; ağır bulut taşıma, uçuşa kalkma ve yolcuların ayrılması yalnızca kendi özne ve yapılarında geçerlidir.

concept_map.definition: Bir yükü kaldırıp taşıyabilmeyi veya üstlenmeyi ve bir öznenin yükselerek harekete geçmesini bildirir. İkinci çizgi kuşun uçuşa kalkmasını, göğün yükselmesini ve yolcuların yüklenip yola koyulmasını kapsar.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi kaldıracak gücü bulmak, onu taşımak veya yük olarak üstlenmektir.
Bir öznenin aşağıdaki konumundan yükselmesi veya kuş gibi harekete ve uçuşa başlamasıdır.
Yolcuların yüklerini alıp bulundukları yerden ayrılarak yolculuğa başlamasıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir yükü kaldırıp taşıma ile yukarı kalkarak harekete geçme çizgilerini bir araya getirir; kuş, gök, bulut ve yolcu örnekleri katılımcıya göre bu iki çizgiyi somutlaştırır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi kişiyi korku veya öfke yüzünden tutan titreme ve silkinişi açıkça tanımlar; genel hareket kararsızlığı değil, duygusal tetikleyicisi bulunan bedensel bir sarsıntı söz konusudur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol insanda korku veya öfkeyle beliren titremeyle sınırlıdır; nesnelerin genel sallanma ve yerinde duramama hali ayrı koldadır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Duygudan doğan titreme temel addır; kişiyi titremenin tutması ve öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi yalnızca ilgili yapılara bağlı anlatımlardır.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanın korku veya öfke yüzünden titremesi, ürpermesi ya da bedensel olarak silkelenmesidir. Durum, kişiyi bir titreme nöbetinin tutması veya öfkenin titremeyle dışa vurulması biçiminde anlatılabilir.

facets.statement: İnsan bedeninde beliren titreme, ürperti veya istemsiz silkiniş halidir.
Titremenin belirleyici nedeni korku ya da öfkedir.
Belirli yapılarda titremenin kişiyi tutması veya kişinin öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar insandaki titreme ve silkinişte birleşir; korku ile öfke başlıca nedenlerdir ve durum hem kişiyi tutan bir nöbet hem öfkenin bedensel belirtisi olarak anlatılır.

error_profile.preserves: Korku veya öfke koşulunu ve bunun doğurduğu bedensel titremeyi birlikte korur.

error_profile.preserves: Öfke nedenini ve onunla birlikte ortaya çıkan titremeyi korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyi hareket ettirip sallandırma, nesnenin bulunduğu yerde kararlı duramaması ve hareketin çıkardığı sesi birlikte verir; bunlar tek bir fiziksel hareket olayının neden, sonuç ve işitsel yönleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol genel fiziksel oynama, kararsızlık ve hareket sesiyle ilgilidir; korku veya öfkeden doğan insana özgü titreme değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım çıplak kolun hareket ettirme, sallanma, yerinde duramama ve hareket sesi anlamlarını kapsar; özel bir yapının anlamı genelleştirilmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi hareket ettirerek yerinden oynatmayı ve onun kararsızca sallanıp bulunduğu yerde duramamasını bildirir; bu hareketin çıkardığı ses de aynı olayın işitsel yönüdür.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi hareket ettirip onun yerinden oynamasına ve sarsılmasına neden olmaktır.
Nesnenin bulunduğu yerde sabit kalmayıp sallanması, oynaması veya düzensiz hareket etmesidir.
Sallanma ve yer değiştirme sırasında çıkan ses, hareket olayının işitsel belirtisi olarak adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar dışarıdan hareket ettirme ile nesnenin kararsızca sallanıp yerinde duramaması üzerinde birleşir; hareketin sesi bu fiziksel olayın ayrılmaz işitsel belirtisi olarak eklenir.
